oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — SLO burn high for /generate v2 (multi-window). burn: 185% (3-window), 120% (1-window). Auto-page triggered. Incident INC-2024-3456

maria: ack, I'm pulling traces and histogram from the last 30m. seeing a mid-tail latency spike at ~600ms p95 -> p99. :eyes:

jon: any 5xx spikes? customers reporting timeouts?

maria: error-rate up from 0.08% -> 0.6% over last 10m, mostly downstream timeouts to model-batcher. No external customer tickets yet but we should assume degraded experience for heavy prompt users.

emma: paging in. grabbing logs for the failing tasks. tagging infra oncall. @saam can you check GPU pool pressure?

saam: looking — dedicated-gpu-pool A has a burst of long-lived KV-cached keys, memory pressure ~82%, some preemption events 10m ago. scheduler logs show increased queue length.

maria: reproduction from traces: long tail appears when sequence-length > 1024 + rare model fallback to variant-quantized. KV cache miss rate increases -> stall.

jon: mitigation plan options: 1) temporary raise SLO alert threshold (stop paging) 2) short policy change to escalate fewer p95 blips 3) immediate rollback to older model variant for /generate v2. Thoughts?

alex: can we do quick fallback to model-v2-stable (non-quant) for gold customers while we investigate? That avoids cluster pressure. I can run a targeted routing change.

maria: agree targeted routing for high-throughput tenants. For platform-level, we should reduce continuous batching window to lower long tail but that increases cost.

emma: I'll take the first handoff for mitigation execution. Oncall rotation: @emma now primary.

oncall-bot: @emma has claimed the pager for INC-2024-3456

emma: ok doing two immediate actions — (A) create a temp routing rule to send tenants with >100qps to model-v2-stable for 15m; (B) adjust alerting to avoid repeat pages for 3-window transient blips.

maria: for (B) propose updating SLO burn paging criteria: previously pages when 3-window burn > 150%. New temp rule: page only when 3-window burn > 200% OR (3-window burn > 150% AND error-rate > 0.5%). That reduces noise when burn is from latency-only with no customer-facing errors.

jon: I like it as a temporary change while we root cause. We should record it in the post-incident actions and revert in 24h unless RCA done.

saam: deploying a dashboard now to track: KV cache miss rate, GPU pool queue length, batch size distribution, per-tenant routing. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/INC-2024-3456

alex: routing patch queued, applying to 12% of traffic first (canary). command: `rwctl route set /generate v2 --model model-v2-stable --selector tenant in (gold,test-canary) --expires 15m`

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-change/1729504402 -> canary 12%

maria: canary looks good so far. error-rate for canary tenants dropped to baseline. overall GPU queue length decreased by ~18% after canary.

emma: updating alert rule temporarily. New alert snippet (applied as temp):

```
alert: SLOBurnMultiWindow
expr: max_over_time(slo_burn/3m[3m:1m]) > 2.0 or (max_over_time(slo_burn/3m[3m:1m]) > 1.5 and increase(error_rate, 3m) > 0.005)
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "SLO burn sustained (temp gating)"
```

emma: note — this is intentionally stricter on paging. I've recorded change in alerting audit.

jon: please also create a ticket to re-evaluate our multi-window policy. Suggestion: add a burn budget guard that factors in total remaining monthly budget before paging heavy alerts. If a service has >20% remaining burn budget, avoid paging for latency-only burns under 2x.

maria: creating follow-up ticket: RDW-INC-3456-ALERT-TUNING. Will include proposed multi-window policy, budget gating, and rollout plan for permanent rule.

saam: quick mitigation summary for customer-impact: degraded latency for heavy prompt tenants, intermittent timeouts for small subset, no broad outage. Upshot: reduced error-rate after routing canary. Recommend customer comms: hold unless we see external tickets.

emma: handoff notes before I go: routing rollback plan ready; alert gating is in place; dashboard saved and shared; next oncall @jon will take post-incident monitoring for 2 hours.

jon: taking follow-up. I will monitor dashboards, confirm rollback window, and coordinate RCA. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2024-3456 status -> mitigated (routing canary successful). Page suppressed by temp alert gating.

maria: postmortem items (short): 1) Investigate KV cache eviction policy for long sequences 2) Add per-tenant queue depth alert to detect tenant-caused pressure 3) Revisit default batching window for long-sequence workloads 4) Implement burn-budget gating in alerter.

jon: agreed. Also add a playbook snippet for targeted routing fallback (`rwctl route set ... --selector`) so the next oncall can act faster.

emma: logging final note: I will remove the temp alert gating in 24h unless RCA complete. Leaving the canary routing to auto-expire at 15m per patch.

alex: thanks all — nice quick containment.

oncall-bot: closing thread: incident updated -> RCA ticket RDW-INC-3456-ALERT-TUNING created.
